data.hypothesis: A two-sided recurrence anchored at exponent zero can eliminate powf calls entirely: powers on each side use at most 32 multiplications, rather than the parent's eight powf seeds and seven-step segments. Accumulating powers in double should limit rounding drift before conversion back to float for the unchanged payoff expression. Whether the added multiplications and double arithmetic improve full-call time, and whether near-boundary payoffs remain within tolerance, require controller measurements.

memory_lessons.applicability: The parent used eight powf seeds and passed its eight reported cases; this contrasting recurrence tests whether those calls can be removed while retaining accuracy.
memory_lessons.claim: The measured parent was valid with mean full-call time 0.304658 s versus the valid baseline's 0.390983 s. Its reported maximum absolute error was 3.0518e-5. These results do not isolate the payoff-generation change's contribution.
memory_lessons.next_experiment: Measure the centered bidirectional recurrence on varied inputs, including cases close to payoff boundaries, and compare full-call timing with the parent.

data.notes: The catalog shows one distinct measured candidate and no recorded incorrect variants. The parent was valid on its reported 8 cases (n=16, 128, 1024, and 131072 across two seeds); this proposal has not been run or validated. Have the controller check varied inputs, especially payoff boundaries, against the fixed tolerance and report full-call timings. The observed parent-versus-baseline timing difference is not an isolated measurement of terminal payoff generation.
transformations: Replace eight block-seeding powf evaluations with a two-sided recurrence anchored at index 32, corresponding to exponent zero.
Use double precision for the recurrence step and accumulator, converting each generated power to float for the existing max(0, X-S*upow) payoff calculation.
Preserve all 64 payoff indices and leave rollback unchanged.
